outlooks.summary: Scattered severe storms are likely today across parts of the southern Plains, Arklatex, Ozarks and lower to mid Mississippi Valley. Damaging wind, hail and a few tornadoes are expected. Isolated severe storms are also possible into the Tennessee Valley.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: A mid/upper-level low is forecast to move from western KS eastward toward the Ozark Plateau by Friday morning. In conjunction with this feature, a surface low is forecast to move from TX northeastward toward the mid MS Valley, and a cold front will move through parts of the southern Plains and eventually into the Ark-La-Miss region.

sections.title: TX northeastward toward the lower/mid MS Valley
sections.text: Extensive convection may be ongoing this morning from parts of TX into AR and southeast OK. Uncertainty remains regarding convective evolution through the day, with potential for early-day storms to persist/intensify through the morning, but also some potential for early activity to diminish and then redevelop along the cold front and/or remnant outflow boundary later. In either case, a corridor of organized convection is expected to evolve by early afternoon from central TX into parts of AR, as large-scale ascent associated with the mid/upper-level low overspreads a moist and unstable environment. MLCAPE of 1500-2500 J/kg and 40-50 kt of effective shear across the warm sector will support organized storms. A mostly cluster or linear mode is expected with convection mostly being focused along the front/outflow, resulting in a primary threat of damaging wind gusts. However, embedded supercells will also be possible, which could pose a threat of hail and a few tornadoes.

sections.title: Southeast MO into western KY and western/middle TN
sections.text: A warm front is forecast to move northward across the region later today, possibly accompanied by a weak frontal wave. Moderate instability and sufficient deep-layer flow/shear will support the potential for isolated supercells near and south of the warm front during the afternoon, if early-day convection does not become too disruptive across this region. Any supercell near the warm front would pose a risk for large hail and a tornado or two.

sections.title: Southeast KS/Northeast OK/Southwest MO/Far northwest AR
sections.text: The primary midlevel vorticity maximum will move through northern OK and southern KS during the afternoon, in conjunction with the synoptic cold front. Moisture return into this region will likely be disrupted by extensive convection to the south/southeast, with little opportunity for diurnal heating/destabilization. However, steep midlevel lapse rates may support a few strong storms capable of hail and gusty winds, especially if heating across this region is stronger than currently anticipated. ..Dean/Wendt.. 05/05/2022

outlooks.summary: Scattered severe storms are likely, mainly during the afternoon into early evening across parts of central to east Texas through the Mid-South. Damaging winds should be the primary hazard, but isolated tornadoes and large hail will also be possible.

sections.title: Central and east TX to the Mid-South
sections.text: The remnants of extensive convective overturning overnight are ongoing across parts of MO/AR/OK. A lead MCV associated with a decaying MCS has reached southeast MO, outpacing most CAM guidance. Flow enhancement attendant to the MCV should largely remain on the cool side of the surface warm front and outpace richer boundary-layer moisture as it tracks into the Lower OH Valley. It appears plausible that trailing convective outflow oriented from northeast to southwest will effectively serve as the primary boundary for afternoon storm development in the Mid-South region of the MS Valley. Steepening low-level lapse rates to its east/south should promote a main threat of scattered damaging wind gusts, with low confidence tornado potential focused near the warm front/outflow intersection. Farther west-southwest, elevated convection over southeast OK spreading east-southeast combined with additional convective development blossoming along the composite surface cold front/outflow into central TX should foster widespread thunderstorms this afternoon. sections.title: Ozark Plateau vicinity
sections.text: Large-scale ascent tied to the primary mid-level vorticity maximum embedded within the upper low over western KS will approach the KS/OK/MO/AR borders region this afternoon. Extensive convective overturning this morning and residual cloudiness will likely mitigate substantial boundary-layer heating. Nevertheless, a plume of steep mid-level lapse rates near the low and adequate deep-layer shear should promote a threat for mainly isolated severe hail during the late afternoon to early evening. ..Grams/Broyles.. 05/05/2022

outlooks.summary: Scattered severe storms are likely, mainly during the afternoon into early evening across parts of central to east Texas through the Mid-South. Damaging winds should be the primary hazard, but isolated tornadoes and large hail will also be possible.

sections.title: Central and east TX to the Mid-South
sections.text: Water-vapor imagery this morning shows an intense mid-level shortwave trough over the central/southern High Plains. The leading edge of strong mid- to upper-level forcing for ascent is overspreading central/eastern OK late this morning. As the mid-level trough progresses east today/tonight, additional thunderstorm activity will result in an extensive area of thunderstorm clusters/bands from central TX northeast into the Mid South/MS Valley. Extensive cloud cover will likely delay/partially inhibit destabilization for parts of the Mid South. However, a rejuvenation of storms is expected with damaging gusts the primary threat with the stronger storms this afternoon/early evening. Farther south ahead of a composite boundary over TX, a very moist airmass sampled by the 12z Corpus Christi, TX raob showed a 17 g/kg lowest 100 mb mean mixing ratio---supporting large buoyancy and thunderstorm activity. Mean flow oriented largely parallel to the boundary has and likely will continue to favor a linear band of strong to severe thunderstorms. As this activity evolves, a mix of linear convective clusters and perhaps an embedded supercell will likely evolve into a QLCS across east TX moving into

sections.title: Ozark Plateau vicinity
sections.text: The aforementioned mid-level disturbance rounding the base of a larger scale trough, will continue east across OK today. Cloud breaks across eastern OK in combination to some modest diurnal heating and cooling mid-level temperatures, will lead to moderate destabilization by early afternoon. Ample mid- to high-level flow/shear will support updraft organization and the propensity for large hail growth with the stronger cores. Despite the presence of rich low-level moisture over a small part of southern OK ahead of the front (north of the northeast TX thunderstorm activity), low-level shear is forecast to remain weak/modest, thereby limiting the tornado risk. ..Smith/Weinman.. 05/05/2022

outlooks.summary: The threat of scattered severe storms will persist through early evening across parts of eastern Texas through the Mid-South. Damaging winds, isolated tornadoes and large hail remain possible. Primary changes at 20Z were to reduce severe probabilities behind the cold front in Texas, and to expand the Slight Risk into Middle TN, south-central KY and northern AL. Also removed the small Slight Risk over eastern OK as the air mass continues to overturn with numerous storms. Isolated hail remains possible over eastern OK. For more information on the Ar/MS/TN area, see mesoscale discussions 661 and 662. And for the eastern OK area, mesoscale discussion 660. ..Jewell.. 05/05/2022 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1130 AM CDT Thu May 05 2022/

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A substantive further increase in thunderstorms appears probable into early afternoon, including the evolution of a gradually organizing cluster of storms with damaging wind gusts becoming the more prominent hazard later this afternoon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An increase in thunderstorm development is ongoing near the Interstate 35 corridor of central Texas. This appears focused near a pre-cold frontal confluence zone (along a wind shift from southwesterly to west-southwesterly around the 850 mb level), aided by increasingly divergent upper flow downstream of large-scale mid/upper troughing pivoting east of the southern Rockies. Breaks in cloud cover preceding this activity will allow for insolation to contribute to weakening of mid-level inhibition. Mixed-layer CAPE already appears on the order of 2000 J/kg, and it appears that large-scale forcing for ascent may support a substantive further increase in convection and upscale growth through early afternoon. Deep-layer shear is strong and supportive of organizing convection, with 30-50 kt southwesterly to west-southwesterly flow in the 850-500 mb layer. This may include a few supercells initially, with 40+ kt southwesterly deep-layer mean flow supporting advection of initial activity toward the Ark-La-Tex, before strengthening rear inflow contributes an eastward/southeastward progression of consolidating outflow later this afternoon. As this occurs, damaging wind gusts will become the more prominent severe hazard after stronger initial storms pose a risk for large hail and perhaps a tornado or two.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Scattered strong thunderstorm development may persist into early afternoon, while spreading eastward across the region. While stronger storms may occasionally pose some risk for severe hail, it is not clear that a severe weather watch is needed. But trends will continue to be monitored.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Mid-level cooling in the exit region of a 50-60+ kt 500 mb jet streak is overspreading a moist pre-frontal environment near the Interstate 35 corridor of Oklahoma. This has contributed to sufficient destabilization to support vigorous thunderstorm development, which will tend to spread eastward/northeastward with the supporting forcing for large-scale ascent through early afternoon. Storms probably are generally rooted within forcing for large-scale ascent associated with warm advection above the boundary-layer, with the near-surface layer across most areas north of the Red River impacted by substantial prior convective outflow. However, strong cloud-bearing layer shear and convectively unstable thermodynamic profiles may remain conducive to the threat for severe hail in stronger cells. Boundary-layer destabilization within the warm sector of a developing surface low could also become a focus for a more substantive severe weather threat later this afternoon across parts of southeastern Oklahoma into the Ark-La-Tex, depending on how things evolve with an evolving convective system across central and northeastern Texas.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The risk of severe thunderstorms will gradually increase and spread east-northeastward this afternoon. A watch may eventually be needed.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest radar data from KLZK shows an expanding cluster of storms spreading east-northeastward across parts of southern AR. Across the pre-convective environment, visible satellite loops show increasing boundary-layer destabilization characterized by deepening horizontal convective rolls amid diurnal heating of a moist airmass (middle/upper 60s surface dewpoints). As the ongoing convection begins to interact with the destabilizing surface-based inflow and large-scale ascent gradually increases across the area, the severe risk will increase. Regional VWP data shows favorable deep-layer flow/shear oriented largely parallel to the ongoing convective cluster, which should continue to favor upscale growth amid minimal CINH. This will generally support a risk for damaging gusts, though any north/south-oriented component of the line could favor a couple mesovortex tornadoes and perhaps isolated large hail. Watch issuance may eventually be needed.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An evolving convective system may further organize, accompanied by potential for increasingly widespread strong wind gusts and perhaps occasional brief tornadoes through 2-4 PM CDT. Trends are being monitored for additional watches downstream.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A pre-cold frontal confluence zone around the 850 mb level has remained the focus for vigorous thunderstorm development across and northeast of the I-35 corridor of central Texas. Increasingly divergent upper flow has supported considerable expansion of cloud tops and precipitation during the past couple of hours, northeast of the Waco vicinity toward the Ark-La-Tex, where a surface cold pool appears to be gradually consolidating. Recent trends in radar imagery suggest that a lower/mid tropospheric mesoscale convective vortex may be in the process of forming to the northwest of Tyler. As this continues, strengthening rear inflow is likely to develop to its southwest and south, contributing to a gradual eastward and southeastward acceleration of the strengthening surface cold pool. Locally strong to severe gusts are already occurring with stronger embedded cells (as evidenced by the gust to 54 kt at Waco TX), and it appears that potentially damaging wind gusts may become more widespread across northeastern Texas into the Ark-La-Tex vicinity through 19-21Z. Given the strengthening cold pool, moderately strong low-level shear and deep moist boundary layer (including lower 70s F dew points), the evolution of transient mesovortices along its leading edge appears possible, accompanied by locally stronger gusts and perhaps occasionally intensifying with brief tornadoes possible. ..Kerr.. 05/05/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The risk of isolated strong to severe storms will be possible over the next couple hours, though watch issuance is not expected at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: In the wake of earlier convection, the boundary-layer has sufficiently recovered across northeast TX into southeast OK -- aided by strengthening large-scale ascent/cooling aloft and lower 60s surface dewpoints. VWP data from SRX shows 55-65 kt 0-6 km bulk shear, with modest veering in the 0-3-km layer and a long/straight mid/upper-level hodograph. These factors could support the risk risk of isolated large hail and locally damaging gusts with northeastward tracking supercell clusters during the next couple hours. While the generally straight hodograph may favor splitting supercells and resultant cell interactions, any longer-lived semi-discrete right-moving supercells that can root in the boundary layer could pose a brief tornado risk owing to 200-250 m2/s2 0-3 km SRH (per SRX VWP data). The anticipated short spatial/temporal nature of the threat will likely preclude watch issuance, though trends will be monitored.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The risk of isolated to widely scattered severe thunderstorms may be increasing this afternoon, and watch issuance will be possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: To the south of a lifting warm front currently draped across parts of KY, diurnal heating of a moist boundary layer (middle/upper 60s dewpoints spreading northward) beneath steep midlevel lapse rates is resulting in a moderately unstable airmass. Regional VWP data shows around 50 kt of midlevel southwesterly flow overspreading south-southwesterly low-level flow -- supporting elongated hodographs with modest low-level veering profiles. Surface pressure falls and related low-level confluence is favoring isolated convective development across parts of western and middle TN, and this activity may increase in intensity and coverage this afternoon. The primary concern will be locally damaging gusts and isolated large hail with northward spreading clusters, though a brief tornado will also be possible owing to near 100 m2/s2 effective SRH. Watch issuance will be possible this afternoon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The risk of large to very large hail, damaging winds, and perhaps a brief tornado continues across Severe Thunderstorm Watch 182.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest radar imagery from KNQA shows a couple intensifying supercells along the leading edge of convective outflow across parts of southeast AR into northwest MS. Regional VWP data shows 40-50 kt of midlevel flow oriented oblique to the outflow boundary, which should continue to favor semi-discrete supercells as they track east-northeastward at around 40 kt. The primary concerns with these storms will be large to very large hail up to 2 inches in diameter and 60-70 mph wind gusts, though a brief tornado cannot be entirely ruled out.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Organizing thunderstorm activity posing a risk for potentially damaging wind gusts and a couple of brief tornadoes remains possible through 6-7 PM CDT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An initial developing mesoscale convective vortex has become better defined across the Texarkana AR area, and appears likely to continue to migrate east-northeastward toward Pine Bluff AR through 22-23Z. A bowing segment evident in radar reflectivities to its south has shown recent weakening trends. However, isolated supercell structures developing near a trailing outflow boundary now just south of Shreveport LA may be maintained another couple of hours by inflow from a lingering narrow corridor of moderately large mixed-layer CAPE south of Shreveport through the Monroe LA vicinity. Otherwise, deep-layer shear remains strong farther to the southwest, and a clustering of storms now north of College Station TX may still intensify further and organize, aided by inflow of seasonably moist air with moderately large CAPE. This could pose increasing risk for potentially damaging wind gusts and perhaps a brief tornado or two across the Huntsville and Lufkin TX vicinities during the next couple of hours. ..Kerr.. 05/05/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat continues across Severe Thunderstorm Watches 0182-0183. Large hail and damaging gusts are the primary threats with the stronger, more sustained storms. The severe threat should persist through sundown, with a gradual weakening trend expected after dark.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Multicellular and transient supercellular storms have been progressing across southern KY and Middle TN over the past few hours while a more sustained supercell structure persists across northern MS. MRMS mosaic radar imagery suggests marginally severe hail has occasionally occurred with the KY/TN storms as they pulse in intensity, with a more defined hail streak ongoing with the MS storm. Across the TN valley, storms are preceded by up to 65F surface dewpoints beneath 7-8 C/km low-level lapse rates, contributing up to 1500 J/kg MLCAPE. 21Z mesoanalysis suggests 30-45 kts of effective bulk shear is in place across the TN Valley, driven by modest speed and directional shear in the 0-3 km layer (as shown by planar hodograph analysis). Given the favorable kinematic and thermodynamic environment in place, occasional bouts of severe hail and damaging gusts should continue with ongoing storms, particularly with the more dominant storms that can avoid harmful cell mergers. This is especially the case for the northern MS storm, which remains somewhat discrete. Damaging gusts may also remain possible with the more linear convection along the MS river which comprises the northern end of an organized MCS. The severe threat should persist through sunset. Thereafter, a gradual weakening trend is likely as the boundary layer stabilizes, as also suggested by the last several runs of the HRRR. ..Squitieri.. 05/05/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat will continue to shift gradually east and south of ww181. At this time a new watch is not anticipated.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Upper trough continues its eastward progression across the central/southern Plains early this evening. Substantial flow extends through the base of this feature across low latitudes which supports the idea that organized convection will spread east of ww181 and potentially sag a bit south over the next few hours. While a mature squall line is noted across northwestern LA into southeast TX, much of this convection is sub-severe with gusty winds less than 50kt. Trailing convection across southern portions of the watch is less linear in nature and appears to be producing marginally severe hail at times, likely a product of steeper lapse rates and higher buoyancy. While isolated hail/wind may continue with this activity for the next few hours, overall trends do not favor extending the watch downstream. ..Darrow.. 05/05/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An isolated severe threat may materialize with the more robust storms that can develop in central Mississippi, just south of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 182. An additional WW issuance is unexpected given the sparse, spatially confined nature of the severe threat outside of the watch area.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A couple of supercell structures have recently materialized across portions of central MS within a low-level confluence axis ahead of a mature MCS. MRMS mosaic radar data shows 30+ dBZ cores exceeding 50 kft, indicative of robust convective growth. Deep-layer shear is a bit stronger across central MS relative to areas farther north, with 50-55 kts of effective bulk shear, driven mainly by stronger speed shear above 700 mb as a mid-level speed max overspreads MS. As such, sustained supercell structures may persist for a couple more hours, posing some threat for severe hail. Damaging gusts may also occur (given mid 80s F surface temperatures and a well-mixed boundary layer/steep low-level lapse rates). After a couple of hours, storms may be overtaken by the line and undercut by the MCS cold pool. Given the anticipated brief and spatially confined nature of the severe threat, a WW issuance is not expected. However, a local extension of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 0182 is possible.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A couple damaging gusts or marginally severe hailstones may accompany the stronger, longer lasting storms. A WW issuance appears unlikely at this time given the short term, isolated nature of the severe threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong to occasionally severe thunderstorms continue to show transient periods of large hail production and damaging gusts per MRMS mosaic and KOHX radar data. The surface airmass ahead of the storms is characterized by upper 70s/low 80s F temperatures and dewpoints around 60 F. Given the presence of a relatively mixed boundary layer and low-level lapse rates, storms may maintain their intensity to produce a couple of damaging gusts/instances of marginally severe hail until sunset. Thereafter, storms should weaken with nocturnal cooling/boundary-layer decoupling. As such, a WW issuance does not appear likely given the short-term duration of the isolated severe threat.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A supercell or two will be possible the next few hours across southeast Louisiana, but a watch does not appear necessary.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storms have formed in the past 1-2 hours across southeast LA, within the warm sector in advance of southeastward-moving outflow boundary. Boundary-layer dewpoints in the low 70s and surface temperatures in the mid-upper 70s are maintaining MLCAPE near 2000 J/kg. Convective inhibition appears to have weakened since the 00z LIX sounding with the approach of a lead/convectively-enhanced shortwave trough moving over the lower MS Valley, and storms will likely persist for a few more hours. The VWP from LIX shows stronger low-level shear (0-1 km SRH near 300 m2/s2 for the observed storm motion from 265 at 30 kt) compared to short-term model forecasts. The combination of this low-level shear with effective bulk shear in excess of 40 kt will favor some supercell structures. Still, there are some limiting factors, such as backing flow in the mid levels which extends into the top of the storm inflow layer (which reduces effective SRH compared to 0-1 km SRH). Also, the outflow boundary moving southeastward will tend to undercut the more discrete storms from north-to-south over the next 2-3 hours. Isolated wind damage/large hail and a brief tornado cannot be ruled out, but the overall severe threat appears too marginal to warrant a watch. ..Thompson.. 05/06/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong/gusty winds appear possible with a line of thunderstorms moving eastward early this morning. Watch issuance is not expected.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A small cluster of thunderstorms has persisted over the past few hours across southeastern LA, aided by ascent from an upper trough centered over the Ozarks. The presence of low to mid 70s surface dewpoints ahead of this convection across coastal MS/AL is supporting around 1000-1500 J/kg of MLCAPE across this area, with minimal convective inhibition noted on latest mesoanalysis estimates. Recent velocity radar imagery from KLIX/KMOB does show some enhanced winds with the northern portion of the cluster, tracking eastward across coastal MS at 0710Z. Although low-level flow is fairly modest, around 20-25 kt, wind fields do strengthen with height to 50+ kt at midlevels. Similar values of deep-layer shear should aid continued convective organization with the line as it moves eastward across southern MS into southern AL and the far western FL Panhandle over the next couple of hours. Isolated strong/gusty winds capable of producing sporadic damage should be the primary threat. There has also been occasional low-level rotation noted within the line, and effective SRH near 100 m2/s2 may be sufficient for a brief tornado. The overall severe threat should be spatially limited to very close to the coast where the greater low-level moisture and boundary-layer instability are present. This cluster should eventually weaken with eastward extent across the western FL Panhandle as it encounters a less unstable airmass.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A line of thunderstorms may continue to produce isolated strong/gusty winds as it moves eastward this morning. Watch issuance is not expected.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A convective cluster has persisted this morning into parts of the FL Panhandle and southern AL. Measured wind gusts associated with this activity have generally remained in the 35-55 mph range over the past couple of hours. The airmass ahead of the line may remain marginally favorable for severe convective gusts to reach the surface for the next hour or two, and isolated strong/gusty winds may be capable of producing occasional tree damage. Still, gradual weakening is anticipated beyond 12Z as these thunderstorms encounter weaker instability and greater convective inhibition with eastward extent into the FL Panhandle ad southwestern GA. Accordingly, watch issuance is not expected.
